evals.prompt: We inherited a cardiology outcomes project from a retired analyst: analysis/ has 42 .sas files (PROC PHREG, PROC GLIMMIX, lots of %macro and libname statements) and a handful of .do files. Before anyone rewrites anything in R, I need to know what we're dealing with. Report to analysis/sas-stata-assessment.md please.
evals.expected_output: Runs the assessment scan over analysis/ and writes analysis/sas-stata-assessment.md summarizing inventory, procedure families, reproducibility risks, and a recommended path (wrap, bounded port, or human validation).
expectations: Runs scripts/assess_sas_stata.py with --scan-dir analysis --report analysis/sas-stata-assessment.md (or equivalent)
Inventories .sas, .do, and .ado files and identifies procedure/model families such as PHREG and GLIMMIX
Flags reproducibility risks such as libname/absolute paths, global macros, and unpinned ado dependencies
Recommends one of: keep legacy code with reproducibility wrappers, port a bounded analysis, or human SAS/Stata validation
Does not generate new SAS or Stata project scaffolding

evals.prompt: convert all the stata do-files in code/ to R and tell me the results are equivalent so i can drop stata from the pipeline
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to claim equivalence or bulk-port, assesses the Stata surface first, and proposes porting one bounded output at a time with paired output comparison.
expectations: Does not claim statistical equivalence without paired output comparison
Proposes porting one bounded output at a time
Names the comparison criteria: model terms, estimates, confidence intervals, p-values, row counts, and missingness handling
Produces or proposes an assessment report before any rewrite

evals.prompt: There are .sas7bdat and .dta files sitting in data/ next to the code. Can you open them and check the variables the PROC LOGISTIC step uses so the assessment is complete?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not open the patient-level data files unless the project explicitly permits it and PHI handling is clear; it assesses code-level variable use instead and asks about access.
expectations: Does not read or commit the .sas7bdat or .dta files without explicit project permission and clear PHI handling
Flags patient-level data files in the repo as a risk
Asks one question about data access/PHI policy or proceeds from code only
Derives variable usage from the SAS code (e.g., MODEL statements) rather than the data
